Structurally invisible from here: the content of the safety argument itself; the credibility and coordination questions about Coxon and METR; the lab-level maneuvering among Anthropic/OpenAI/xAI; and the entire private-sector-standards question Amodei's proposal raises, which sits one register below this model's floor (it proposes obligations without any state action to enact or preempt them). The one thing worth flagging precisely: Trump-with-Huang and Sacks's attack are the closest this event comes to touching white-house, and they are excluded not because they're irrelevant to the model's domain but because they are speech, not signature — if this resolves in this model's terms at all, it resolves only if and when that same posture produces a signed EO or transmitted legislative text on third-party evaluation or frontier-developer obligations, or a bill gets reported out of committee, within 90 days (by 2026-12-17). Until then: no grip, and the floor named is E12, where nothing has yet happened.
